text:
ravi: Thanks all — quick follow-up from today's all-hands on serving/kernel roadmap. I promised a short open thread for questions about pipelined ops, batching/caching tradeoffs, and kernel prioritization. Drop questions here and we'll answer through EOD.

liz: Thanks, Ravi. Could you clarify the priority order for kernel work this quarter? Are we focusing quantization kernels first or sparse attention optimizations?

ravi: Short answer: quantization-first for v1 because it gives biggest unit-cost wins. Sparse attention is a Q3 candidate once we have stable 4-bit paths. We'll publish a short RFC by next week. @kevin will add timeline.

kevin: yup — publishing RFC Monday. Current plan: (1) int8/4-bit fast paths, (2) fused attention matmul kernels, (3) sparse ops experiment. ETA for phase 1 rollout to canary is late May.

sam: For batching — are we changing the default batch window to 10ms for hosted? We had some regressions at 20ms in internal tests.

anya: We saw tail-latency regressions at 20ms for short prompts. 10ms reduced p99 by ~60ms but throughput dropped 8%. We want to make the window adaptive per route.

liz: Adaptive window is the goal. Short-term: lower default to 12ms and enable per-route override in console. Ops will monitor for cost impact.

devops-bot: deployment scheduled: canary/adaptive-batcher v2 -> infra1 at 2025-05-08T02:30Z :rocket:

ravi: KV cache eviction heuristic: plan is LRU with weighted age for multi-model tenants. Any objections?

sam: LRU-weighted seems fine. Question — should we weight by recent token-savings estimate (i.e., how many tokens cached times average reuse)?

kevin: Good idea. We're prototyping a lightweight metric: 'estimated saved tokens per second' for each KV entry. If > threshold, bump priority. It's in the RFC.

anya: Performance ask: when we probe new kernel variants, can we expose microbenchmarks in console so teams can pick configs? Even a small table for latency/cost tradeoffs.

liz: Agree. We'll add per-kernel microbench results to the model card UI. Product will scope the UX.

sam: Tiny follow-up — any plan for multi-GPU KV synchronization? That's causing some canary bumps.

kevin: Working on async KV sync prototype that shards minibatches to GPU-local caches and converges in background. Prototype results look promising; won't be in phase1.

ravi: Great thread — I'll collect these and post the RFC + timeline link. If you need to discuss offline, ping me or @liz. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/docs/rfcs/serving/order-1955554321

kevin: added follow-up issue for per-route batch window defaults: INT-4821

anya: +1, thanks.
